steThemes: Human-machine teaming in defence and critical infrastructure

Russia stays a sanctions and compliance watchpoint, not a market.

conditions.name: China-Taiwan tensions
conditions.transmission: Cross-strait escalation could disrupt Taiwan operations and Asian supply chains, tighten technology controls, and change defence demand across the region.

conditions.name: Semiconductor and HBM prices
conditions.transmission: Memory and chip price rises could squeeze project margins and bid validity, and raise AI-infrastructure and product costs across the business areas.

conditions.name: GPU availability
conditions.transmission: Constrained GPU supply or allocation could delay AI-enabled products and data-centre projects even where budget exists, and favour smaller models and edge designs.
watchIndicators: Vendor concentration across GPU, memory and packaging

conditions.name: Frontier AI capability jumps
conditions.transmission: A step change in model capability could speed up AI-enabled cyber attacks and product cycles, and bring new competitors, while opening work in secure, governed autonomy and AI assurance.

conditions.name: AI regulation
conditions.transmission: New AI rules could add assurance and liability requirements to AI-enabled products and services, and could favour sovereign or certified deployments.
watchIndicators: US federal and state AI rules

conditions.name: Quantum computing milestones
conditions.transmission: Progress toward a cryptographically relevant quantum computer could shorten the window to migrate long-life defence, aviation and infrastructure systems to post-quantum cryptography, and opens quantum-safe and quantum-sensing work.
referenceSources: Global Risk Institute Quantum Threat Timeline
